mr_title: consumeSubQuery should not drop leading combinators
mr_description:
Refactored so that it eats until a combinator is seen after non-combinator content, and returns it all.

And corrected unit tests that were incorrectly relying on that behavior.

Note that a leading combinator will combine against the root element, which is either the Document, or the context element.

expected_issues.title: Sub-query does not stop at a combinator after an attribute or group clause
expected_issues.description:
seenNonCombinator is only set for plain characters, so a sub-query that starts with a (...) or [...] clause never stops at the next combinator.

consumeSubQuery() sets seenNonCombinator only in the final else branch. When the sub-query starts with an attribute selector or a parenthesised clause, the flag stays false and the following combinator is appended instead of ending the sub-query, so selectors such as `:has([href] > p)` or `[attr] p` inside a sub-query are parsed with the wrong structure. Upstream fix: set the flag for every non-combinator clause.
